title: The Rich Man and Lazarus
reflectionText: A great chasm stood between them after death. During their lives, Lazarus had been laid at the rich man's gate, longing for what fell from his table. Abraham pointed back to Moses and the prophets. What are they asking us to hear while mercy is still possible?
editorialNotes: PAL Daily supervised production 2026-07-24, Batch C (gap CG13). Luke 16:19-31, the Rich Man and Lazarus, absent both lanes. SHORT only, WEB 300w / KJV 290w. Per owner direction the parable is rendered exactly with NO afterlife commentary in either direction: 'Hades'/'hell' (WEB/KJV lane words), 'Abraham's side'/'Abraham's bosom', the 'great chasm/gulf fixed', and 'this flame' are given as the text gives them, without explaining or systematizing them into doctrine. The reversal (16:25), the fixed gulf (16:26), the five brothers (16:27-28), and the closing 'neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead' (16:31) are all kept; the story ends on 16:31. KJV narration lightly restructured to avoid verbatim reproduction while preserving the essential dialogue and KJV register. TEXT DRAFT — AWAITING ADAM AND CHATGPT REVIEW. REV 2026-07-24 (owner review): reflection replaced (prior added unstated 'close enough to touch' / 'stepped past him every day'; the parable states only that Lazarus was laid at the gate and longed for the crumbs).
